title: :alembic: Secret change for other project
description:
In another project, I want to customise the angles of ticks and labels. 
However, I don't want to advertise this to legendry users. 
So I'm being real sneaky about it and not putting out a news bullet for this experiment.
Essentially thing happening here is that in stack configurations where primitive ticks is followed by primitive labels, and keys have a `theta` column, the tick is oriented with the theta angle and the labels follow that tick.

title: ✨ Manual legend: `guide_legend_manual()`
description:
This PR aims to fix #88.

Briefly, it allows the creation of a `guide_legend_base()` variant where all scale/training is under user control.
@brunomioto as you suggested this in tidyverse/ggplot2#6386, is there any chance I can get you to confirm this would solve the issue?
You can download this PR using: `pak::pak("teunbrand/legendry#109")`

Example:

``` r
devtools::load_all("~/packages/legendry/")
#> ℹ Loading legendry
#> Loading required package: ggplot2

ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  guides(foobar = guide_legend_manual(
    labels = c("foo", "bar"),
    colour = c(NA, "#222222"),
    fill   = c("#d8d8d8", NA),
    layers = geom_col()
  ))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/0FoCZP9.png)<!-- -->

title: ✨ Subtitles for `guide_legend_cross()`
description:
This PR aims to fix #79.

It adds `row_title` and `col_title` arguments in `guide_legend_cross()`.

Based on reprex from issue:

``` r
devtools::load_all("~/packages/legendry/")
#> ℹ Loading legendry
#> Loading required package: ggplot2
library(dplyr)

set.seed(0)
df = expand.grid(x=1:5, tag1 = c("+", "-"), tag2=c("+", "-")) |>
  mutate(y = runif(n()))

shared_legend <- legendry::guide_legend_cross(
  key = "auto", title = NULL,
  col_title = "Condition",
  row_title = "Test"
)

ggplot(df) +
  aes(x = x, y = y, fill=tag1, group=tag1, alpha=tag1==tag2) +
  geom_col(position = 'dodge') +
  scale_alpha_manual(values=c(0.5, 1)) +
  guides(alpha = shared_legend, fill  = shared_legend)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/cPPW3Gg.png)<!-- -->

<sup>Created on 2025-09-27 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

title: :bug: Preserve label order in `key_group_split()`
description:
This PR aims to fix #100.

Reprex from issue, note correct order of D3, D6, D10.

``` r
library(tidyverse)
devtools::load_all("~/packages/legendry/")
#> ℹ Loading legendry

set.seed(123)

df <- tibble(
  umap_1 = rnorm(100),
  umap_2 = rnorm(100),
  sample = rep(c(
    "Control D3",
    "Control D6",
    "Control D10",
    "Treated D3",
    "Treated D6",
    "Treated D10"
  ), length.out = 100)
) %>%
  mutate(
    sample = factor(sample, levels = c(
      "Control D3",
      "Control D6",
      "Control D10",
      "Treated D3",
      "Treated D6",
      "Treated D10"
    ))
  )

palette <- c(
  "Control D3" = "#377eb8",
  "Control D6" = "#6baed6",
  "Control D10" = "#deebf7",
  "Treated D3" = "#e41a1c",
  "Treated D6" = "#fb8072",
  "Treated D10" = "#fee0d2"
)

ggplot(df, aes(umap_1, umap_2)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = sample)) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = palette,
    guide = guide_legend_cross(
      key = key_group_split(sep = " "),
      swap = TRUE
    )
  )
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/gPuWs72.png)<!-- -->

title: :bug: Avoid `new_aes()` and `class_mapping()`
description:
Under ggplot2 3.5.x series, we reimplemented `new_aes()`. This gave malformed classes in ggplot2 4.0.0, so we used `class_mapping()` instead. However, using `utils::getFromNamespace()` to grab `class_mapping()` led the R CMD check to believe that the `S7::new_object()` that is used in the `class_mapping()` constructor originated from legendry. This is not the case, but inconvenienced CRAN checks regardless (hence #97).

To solution is to simplify and use `aes()` itself to construct mappings, which eliminates the need for `new_aes()` and `class_mapping()` altogether.

title: :bug: `<AsIs>` variables in keys
description:
This PR aims to fix #45.

Briefly, it attempts to preserve `<AsIs>` variables better. For standard keys, excluding censoring is sufficient to let this work as intended. For other keys, we need to transform AsIs variables from the [0, 1] range back to the limits, as we cannot mix regular and AsIs variables when interleaving.

Reprex based on issue:

``` r
devtools::load_all("~/packages/legendry/")
#> ℹ Loading legendry
#> Loading required package: ggplot2

data.frame(x = 0:1, y = 0:1) |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(.51, NA), expand = c(0, 0), oob = scales::oob_keep,
    guide = compose_stack("axis", guide_axis_base(
      key = key_manual(I(.5), label = "I(.5)"),
      theme = theme_guide(
        ticks.length = unit(1.5, "cm"),
        ticks = element_line(arrow = arrow())
      )
    ))
  )
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/bpE48EU.png)<!-- -->

<sup>Created on 2025-02-15 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

title: ✨ Dendrograms
description:
This PR aims to fix #33.

Examples of usage:

``` r
devtools::load_all("~/packages/legendry/")
#> ℹ Loading legendry
#> Loading required package: ggplot2
clust <- hclust(dist(scale(USArrests)), "ave")
var_clust <- hclust(dist(scale(t(USArrests))), "ave")

long_arrests <- data.frame(
  state = rownames(USArrests)[row(USArrests)],
  variable = colnames(USArrests)[col(USArrests)],
  value = as.vector(scale(USArrests))
)

ggplot(long_arrests, aes(variable, state, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_y_dendro(clust) +
  scale_x_dendro(var_clust) +
  guides(
```
